result.title: Poisoning-Based Backdoors Are Not Cryptographic
result.summary: To defend against backdoor attacks on neural networks, the defender must identify the verifier function that determines whether an input is a trigger, rather than rejecting individual triggers in isolation, since an attacker can generate new triggers satisfying the same verifier faster than they can be blocked. If a backdoor verifier could be installed with the asymmetry of a cryptographic authentication scheme, in which only the attacker can produce trigger inputs while the defender cannot reverse-engineer the verifier from observations, learning-based defense would be impossible in principle. We show that no such asymmetry can arise from poisoning-based installation, in which the only verifier-dependent input to training is a poisoned dataset. The argument is a reduction. A training procedure that installs a verifier from poisoned data, so that the backdoor fires on unseen triggers while benign behavior is preserved, is itself a learner for that verifier. Any verifier that is computationally hard to learn is therefore impossible to install through poisoning, and any verifier that poisoning can install is reconstructible by a white-box defender holding comparably many labeled trigger observations. A complementary argument shows that a secret key supplied to the model at inference is observable to the same defender. The result takes representative trigger observations as given and concerns when the backdoor fires rather than what it does. Experiments on instruction-tuned large language models confirm the dichotomy, with no configuration yielding a backdoor that is both effective for the attacker and irrecoverable for the defender.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用归约论证表明：基于投毒安装的后门验证器不具备密码学式不对称性——能仅凭投毒数据安装验证器的训练过程本身就是该验证器的学习器，因此在指令微调大模型上攻击有效性与防御者不可恢复性无法兼得。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「能安装即能被学习」的归约形式，可能可供核查 latent 轨迹训练中监督能安装哪些推理行为、分析者能否从观察中恢复内部判据，但与视觉证据筛选和 latent 状态本身无直接联系。
